reason: Fresh independent validation proved corrected M5 core requires live runtime/application injection and truthful Windows cleanup evidence before M5 can close. This additive amendment grants only those post-core paths; frozen M0 semantics remain unchanged.
retainedAuthority: All M0 freezes, M1-M8 rules, and M2-M7 amendment terms remain authoritative except this explicit M5 ownership correction.

globalRules.coreFreeze: The ten M5 core paths committed at sourceRevision are complete one-touch ownership and may not be edited by live-wiring workers.
globalRules.generatedLock: engine/Cargo.lock remains integration-owner generated state and is outside worker ownership.
globalRules.legacy: All Node/Python legacy runtime paths remain read-only evidence until M7.
globalRules.membrane: No worker may read or modify Membrane.
globalRules.execution: All external execution remains argv-only, policy-controlled, bounded, receipt-backed, and effects-owned.
globalRules.qualification: This amendment does not assert M6 qualification or authorize M7 deletion.

M5.dependencyRule: Both disjoint live-wiring lanes start only from completedCoreRevision. M5 closes only after integration verification proves runtime reachability and Windows cleanup truth.
M5.interfaceRule: ContextRequest carries optional Arc<dyn ExternalProjectTool>; Scheduler injects it into ProviderContext; NativeApplication binds it on every Invoke, Run, RunRequest, custom RunSource, and cancellation path. Runtime and SDK never construct an executor or evaluate policy.
M5.cancellationRule: Application and scheduler cancellation/deadline paths signal the active provider/effect future, await bounded cleanup instead of dropping it, preserve returned terminal evidence, and force incomplete cancellation/timeout truth. Non-cooperative cleanup remains bounded and explicitly unconfirmed.
M5.windowsRule: kill_succeeded and process-tree evidence report actual cleanup truth for normal exit, timeout, cancellation, and output-limit paths.
